clue.text: Stupidly keel over with anger, missing large tree

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it in a muddled way, so the letters are jumbled
missing tells us a letter is to be left out of the jumbled letters

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone in a fury collapses foolishly, an image of rage getting the better of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool the letters of KEEL OVER and ANGER, take away the L that 'large' names, and rearrange the remaining twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The evergreen oak, or holm oak, is a species of oak that keeps its leaves all year.

clue.text: Rule out former partner getting idea about daughter

parts.note: an ex is a former husband, wife or partner

indicators.note: about means the idea word goes around the daughter letter

parts.note: a clue is a hint or idea of the answer
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an ex who has had a notion concerning their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude something is to rule it out, a straightforward synonym for barring from consideration.

clue.text: Yes, cats playing can give joy

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters frolicking about and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: Playful cats can make anyone happy, says the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is a state of overwhelming happiness, an intense form of delight.

clue.text: American soldier eats a blue biscuit

indicators.note: the soldier eating something means it takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a GI is a US army soldier
blue jokes are ribald or risqué

explanation.surface: A US soldier munches a mouldy or saucy biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour, or mould on the biscuit, but here means smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: A Garibaldi is a British biscuit of currants squashed between thin layers of pastry-like dough, named after the Italian general.

clue.text: Show featuring mediocre ventriloquist? Just the opposite!

indicators.note: featuring says one thing contains another
just the opposite turns it round: the answer is featured in the words mediocre ventriloquist, not the reverse

explanation.surface: A talent show that includes a not-very-good ventriloquist act.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the show contains the ventriloquist; the exclamation flips this, so the show's name sits inside 'mediocrE VENTriloquist'.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an organised occasion such as a show or competition.

clue.text: Everyone, say, at home, turned up to see celebrity chef?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: everyone means all
say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.
at home means in

explanation.surface: Everybody stayed in to see a famous TV cook turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella Lawson is a well-known British television cook and food writer.

clue.text: One might take off proportion of unfair tax, ideally

indicators.note: a proportion of something is just a part, so the answer is a run of letters within these words

explanation.surface: Reads like a remark on a fair share of tax, ideally.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'unfAIR TAX Ideally'; 'take off' is meant in the aviation sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An air taxi is a small plane hired for short trips, which naturally takes off from a runway.

clue.text: Hangover cure? Go for this, almost, with head spinning

indicators.note: a spinning head sends the letters whirling into a new order
almost means the word this loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Advice for a hungover drinker whose head is spinning: go for this remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims THIS to THI; mix GO, FOR, THI and HEAD together.
explanation.definitionFit: The hair of the dog is an idiom for another alcoholic drink taken to ease the effects of the previous night.

clue.text: One who makes a claim — and one who copies an email?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who alleges wrongdoing
second meaning: someone who uses the cc (carbon copy) field

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as A + CC + USER, cc being the carbon-copy line of an email.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser charges someone with an offence, asserting that they did wrong.

clue.text: English garden slightly altered: this means it's time to begin fencing

definitions.text: this means it's time to begin fencing

indicators.note: altered means changed in arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An English garden with a few changes, so that the fencing can begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing' suggests putting up garden fences, but it is the sword sport; only GARDEN is reordered, after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the call in the sport of fencing telling opponents to take guard before a bout starts.

clue.text: Final moment with volunteer — he cracked up touring hospital

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the hospital letter
something cracked up is broken into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A volunteer breaks down at the last minute while visiting a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked up' looks like the volunteer's breakdown in the surface, but it is the signal to rearrange; 'touring' then wraps that mix around H.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh hour is an idiom for the latest possible time before a deadline.

clue.text: Plant that's mentioned in muffled conversation?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a garden plant with edible pink stalks
second meaning: the word stage extras repeat to simulate background murmur

explanation.walkthrough: Actors in crowd scenes traditionally mutter this word to sound like indistinct chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is a vegetable grown for its tart stalks and also stands for meaningless background talk or nonsense.

clue.text: End of harvest — bad period for ploughman's work

indicators.note: end of means take only the final letter of harvest

parts.note: feeling bad means feeling ill
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A poor end to the harvest makes a hard season for the farm worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the cultivation of land by ploughing and harrowing, the labour of a ploughman.

clue.text: Cook claims that is burning

indicators.note: claims is read as takes in, so the cooking word holds the other letters

parts.note: to fry is one way to cook
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A chef insists that something is on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiery means blazing or aflame, synonymous with being on fire.

clue.text: Unfinished lute I crave, needing renovation: it could be rewarding

indicators.note: something needing renovation must be rebuilt, so the letters are put in a new order
unfinished means the word lute loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A musician longs for a half-made lute that will need restoring and might pay off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative means producing profit, so a lucrative venture pays well.

clue.text: Part in sitcom for terrible dummy

indicators.note: part in means the answer is a stretch of letters lying inside the following words

explanation.surface: A role in a sitcom goes to a dreadful, wooden actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dummy' suggests a poor actor, but it is the British word for a baby's pacifier.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a baby's comforter is a soother or pacifier, also called a dummy.

clue.text: Room for plants in that woman's pub? I hesitate

parts.note: her is the possessive for that woman
a bar is a pub
um is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone at her pub wonders, with some hesitation, whether it has space for greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbarium is a collection of dried plant specimens, or the room or building housing it.

clue.text: Genine sex appeal unknown, in truth

parts.note: the clue's misspelling of genuine, which means real
it is old slang for sex appeal
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Real attractiveness is a mystery, in truth.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'Genine' for 'genuine'; IT for sex appeal dates from the 1920s film star Clara Bow, the 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality is the state of things as they actually are, the facts or the actual state.

clue.text: Hound the setter for money in Kabul?

parts.note: the Afghan hound is a long-haired breed of dog
the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: Seems to ask whether a dog breed and a setter would fetch money in Afghanistan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like another dog breed beside 'Hound', but it is the puzzle's compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: The afghani is the currency of Afghanistan, whose capital city is Kabul.

clue.text: In hoop-la, I throw a braided item

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fairground player tossing a braided ring in hoop-la.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'hooP-LA I Throw'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plait is a length of hair or rope formed by interweaving three or more strands.

clue.text: May be drunk: could be carried, rejecting last of beer

indicators.note: rejecting means the letter named next is thrown out

parts.note: portable means able to be carried

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of beer

explanation.surface: Someone may be tipsy but could still be carried home, having turned down the dregs of the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable describes water or other liquid that is safe to consume.

clue.text: Is consumed by a desire for the taste of ouzo?

indicators.note: being consumed by means being swallowed up inside the other letters

parts.note: a need is a desire or want

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone is consumed by longing for a Greek drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouzo is a Greek spirit flavoured with anise seed, giving its liquorice taste.

clue.text: Dough initially torn and pulled

indicators.note: initially picks only the first letter of dough

parts.note: ragged means torn or tattered

explanation.surface: A baker's dough is torn apart and stretched.
explanation.definitionFit: Dragged means hauled or pulled along with effort.

clue.text: After party, speed regularly administered

indicators.note: after means the party piece comes first, followed by the next one

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of speed, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Following a party, drugs are handed out at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' reads as the drug, which suits the surface, but only its alternate letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosed means given a measured quantity of medicine, as a patient is administered a drug.

clue.text: Cut first bit off fullest-flavoured bird

indicators.note: cut first bit off means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: most rich means having the fullest flavour

explanation.surface: Instructions for trimming the richest-tasting cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fullest-flavoured' gives MOST RICH, two words written as one; drop its M.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless African bird, the largest living species of bird.

clue.text: Axes using technology to infuse refined sugar

indicators.note: to infuse means to go into something, so the technology letters are placed inside
refined sugar is processed, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: IT stands for information technology

explanation.surface: A technical process for infusing refined sugar into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like chopping tools; in musicians' slang an axe is a guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: Axe is rock-musician slang for an electric guitar, so axes are a band's instruments.

clue.text: Dramatic moment framed, as gold is added onto index

indicators.note: the gold letters are added onto the end of the index word

parts.note: an index is a table, as in a list or table of contents
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A dramatic moment is captured as a gold border is fixed to an index card.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene, or a pause in a play where actors freeze as in a picture.

clue.text: Child yearned to rebuild engine component

indicators.note: rebuilding something means putting its parts together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A child longs to rebuild a part from an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: The cylinder head sits on top of an engine block, closing the cylinders and housing the valves.
